## Description

High throughput toxicokinetics ("HTTK") is the
combination of in vitro TK data and generic mathematical models to
predict absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion by the
body, as described by [Pearce et al. (2017)](https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v079.i04) and
[Breen et al. (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1080/17425255.2021.1935867).
Chemical-specific in vitro TK data are available for only a few thousand
chemicals. [Dawson et al. (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.0c06117) and
[Honda et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.14573/altex.2403271)
developed a series of random forest Quantitative Structure-Property Relationship (QSPR)
models to predict these parameters for a broader set of chemicals.
The QSPR models require structure-derived chemical-specific descriptors from
[Padel](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcc.21707) and [OPERA](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13321-018-0263-1).
Assuming the user can generate these descriptors, or has access to a database of pre-generated
descriptors, then this package can be used to calculate the HTTK parameter Clint (intrinsic hepatic clearance),
fup (fraction unbound in plasma), and Papp (apparent membrane permeability in a Caco-2 experiment).

## Getting Started

For an introduction to R, see Irizarry (2022) "Introduction to Data Science":
<http://rafalab.dfci.harvard.edu/dsbook/getting-started.html>

For an introduction to toxicokinetics, with examples in "httk", see Ring (2021) in the "TAME Toolkit":
<https://uncsrp.github.io/Data-Analysis-Training-Modules/toxicokinetic-modeling.html>

### Dependencies

* Users will need the freely available R statistical computing language: <https://www.r-project.org/>
* Users will likely want a development environment like RStudio: <https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/>
* If you get the message "Error in library(X) : there is no package called 'X'" then you will need to install that package:
	From the R command prompt: install.packages("X")
  Or, if using RStudio, look for 'Install Packages' under the 'Tools' tab.
* Note that R does not recognize fancy versions of quotation marks that curve
toward each other.
If you are cutting and pasting from software like Word or Outlook you may need
to replace the quotation marks that curve toward each other with ones typed by
the keyboard.

### Installing R package "httkqsprs"

The package is not on CRAN. Install it from the repository, pointing at the
`httkqsprs` subdirectory:
```{r install_httkqsprs, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github(
  "ULRI-CIRI/dawson2021-httkqspr",
  subdir = "httkqsprs"
)
```

### "Write Privileges" On Your Personal Computer

Depending on the account you are using and where you want to install the
package on that computer, you may need "permission" from your local file system
to install the package. See the help here:

<https://stackoverflow.com/questions/42807247/installing-package-cannot-open-file-permission-denied>

and here:

<https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/general-problem-installing-any-r-package-0bf1f9ba-ead2-6335-46ec-190f6af75e44>

### Delete all objects from memory:
It is a bad idea to let variables and other information from previous R
sessions float around, so we first remove everything in the R memory.
```{r clear_memory, eval = TRUE}
rm(list=ls())
```

### Load the HTTK data, models, and functions
```{r load_httk, eval = TRUE}
library(httkqsprs)

# Check what version you are using
packageVersion("httkqsprs")
```

## Examples

* Predict Clint, Fup, and Papp from OPERA and PaDEL descriptor files

`generate_preds()` reads a pair of descriptor files that you supply and returns
predictions for all three endpoints. Both files must sit in `input.folder` and
share a common label: for the label `"NewHTTK_April_2026"` the OPERA file is
`NewHTTK_April_2026-smi_OPERA2.9Pred.csv` and the PaDEL file is
`NewHTTK_April_2026_QSAR-ready_smi_PadelDesc.csv`. Descriptors may come from
running OPERA and PaDEL yourself or from a database of pre-generated
descriptors, as long as they are exported in that file layout.

The chunk below is not evaluated when the vignette is built because the
descriptor files are supplied by you; point `input.folder` at the directory
holding them and run it yourself.
```{r make_predictions, eval = FALSE}
out <- generate_preds(
  "NewHTTK_April_2026",
  input.folder = "path/to/descriptor/files",
  output.folder = tempdir()
)
# Clint values:
head(out$Clint$output[, c("MoleculeID", "ClintPredictBin_MD", "Outlier")])
# Fup values:
head(out$Fup$output[, c("MoleculeID", "Fup.RF.pred", "Outlier")])
# Papp values:
head(out$Papp$output[, c("MoleculeID", "Pab.Class.Pred", "Pab.Pred.AD")])
```

Chemicals missing a descriptor that Clint or Fup requires are excluded from
`$output` and returned in `$missing` instead, for example `out$Clint$missing`.
Papp imputes missing descriptors rather than excluding chemicals, so
`out$Papp$missing` is `NULL`.

* Predict from a descriptor frame you assembled yourself

`generate_preds()` is a convenience wrapper over the CSV layout above. The
package's actual interface is a data frame: each of `calc_clint()`,
`calc_fup()`, and `calc_papp()` takes one data frame keyed on a `MoleculeID`
column, with one column per descriptor. Use this when your descriptors come
from a database, an API, or any source that is not the two-CSV layout.

`required_descriptors()` reports exactly which descriptor columns an endpoint
needs, split by the source they come from. OPERA names carry a `_pred` suffix
and PaDEL names do not, so the two sets never collide and can be merged into
one wide frame.
```{r required_descriptors, eval = TRUE}
needs <- required_descriptors("fup")
needs$opera
needs$padel
```

Retrieve those columns however you like, assemble them into a frame, and
predict. Extra columns are ignored, so one wide frame covering all three
endpoints can be passed to all three functions.
```{r calc_from_frame, eval = FALSE}
# `descriptors` is your data frame: MoleculeID plus the descriptor columns
fup <- calc_fup(descriptors)
fup$output # chemicals with a complete descriptor set
fup$missing # chemicals dropped for a missing descriptor
```

If a required column is absent the function stops and names the columns it
could not find, rather than predicting from partial inputs.

`read_descriptor_csvs()` is exported for the middle case: you want the CSV
layout read and merged for you, but you want the descriptor frame rather
than all three sets of predictions.
```{r read_descriptor_csvs, eval = FALSE}
descriptors <- read_descriptor_csvs(
  "NewHTTK_April_2026",
  input.folder = "path/to/descriptor/files",
  operapostfix = "-smi_OPERA2.9Pred.csv",
  padelpostfix = "_QSAR-ready_smi_PadelDesc.csv"
)
calc_papp(descriptors)$output
```
